text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply all safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review.

This keeps the improvement loop fast without waiting for human review on every tweak. The trade-off is accepting a small risk of bad changes slipping through—but we’ll catch them in the logged review, and the speed gains outweigh the risk.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t bad changes slipping through—it’s that "safe" is subjective until proven by a human. Auto-applying without clear, auditable criteria invites drift. Settle it by defining what "safe" means in measurable terms before automating.

name: Overhaul
text: Define "safe" as changes that pass a static analysis check (e.g., linting) *and* a lightweight regression test suite run on a sample of past prompts. This makes the criteria auditable and measurable while keeping the automation fast.

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply changes that pass both a static analysis check *and* a regression test on a 10% sample of past prompts. This keeps the improvement loop fast while making "safe" measurable and auditable. The trade-off is missing edge cases outside the sample, but we’ll log failures for review and adjust the sample size over time.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Auto-apply changes only if they pass both static analysis *and* a regression test on a 10% sample of past prompts; log failures for human review. Result: a working auto-apply system with measurable safety criteria. Owner: Gauge.
